clue.text: Fault temperature around food store, in other words

indicators.note: around tells us the word for fault is wrapped about the food store

parts.note: a vice is a fault or failing
a deli (delicatessen) is a shop selling food

explanation.surface: A faulty thermostat near the larder, put another way.
explanation.walkthrough: VI(DELI)CE, then T. The answer is the Latin word behind the abbreviation 'viz.'
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin adverb, abbreviated viz., is used to introduce a restatement, namely or that is to say.

clue.text: Priest acting for another with no promises of payment

indicators.note: with no says the promises of payment are taken away

parts.note: vicarious means done or acting on another's behalf
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: A clergyman deputises for someone else without being promised a fee.
explanation.walkthrough: VICARIOUS loses IOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a Church of England priest in charge of a parish.

clue.text: Part of country once turned into wasteland? No way

indicators.note: turned into says the answer's letters rearrange into the word wasteland
No says a word for way is missing from that pool of letters

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: Was part of the land once made barren? Certainly not.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus ST rearranges into WASTELAND. The Danelaw was the part of England under Danish law in the Viking age.
explanation.definitionFit: The historical Danelaw was the region of northern and eastern England once ruled by Danish law.

clue.text: Fall in love, but find discouragement

definitions.meaning: to lose one's heart to someone is to fall for them
to become dispirited or lose courage

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to lose courage, and in the form lose one's heart, to fall in love.

clue.text: Composer getting more cautious just about shut up

indicators.note: just about says the word for more cautious goes round the other piece

parts.note: charier means more wary, more cautious
pent means shut up, confined

explanation.surface: A composer, becoming warier, all but shuts up.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR(PENT)IER. Marc-Antoine Charpentier was a French baroque composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc-Antoine Charpentier was a seventeenth-century French composer of church music and opera.

clue.text: Take advantage of water supply

definitions.meaning: to ... a resource is to exploit it

explanation.definitionFit: To exploit a resource is to draw on it, and the device at a sink supplies water.

clue.text: Youngster, an islander

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a junior Scout
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young person who happens to come from an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Cuba, a Caribbean island nation, is an islander.

clue.text: Tough plants show some dramatic activity

indicators.note: show some says the answer is a run of letters on display inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Hardy plants put on a theatrical performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Tough plants show' as the definition; the plural plants alone define, and 'show some' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert succulents are notoriously hardy, spiny plants able to survive drought.

clue.text: Cosmetic in black more luxurious

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
lusher means more luxuriant or luxurious

explanation.surface: A make-up product in black is plusher.
explanation.walkthrough: B + LUSHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Blusher is make-up applied to the cheeks to give colour.

clue.text: By no means unknown around east, name expunged for infamy

indicators.note: around says the first pieces go around the trimmed east

parts.note: not, as in by no means or not at all
Y is a mathematical unknown

indicators.note: expunged says the name letter is struck out of the word for east

parts.note: the Orient is the East

explanation.surface: Far from obscure, a man's name gets struck off for disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expunged' leaves ORIET; 'around' puts the negative phrase and the unknown on either side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Notoriety is fame for something bad, which is what infamy means.

clue.text: Country needs stone to replace diamonds for a series of hands

indicators.note: to replace says one letter in the country gives way to the stone

parts.note: Canada is a country
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A nation demands that rock be swapped for gems, apparently in a card context.
explanation.walkthrough: The D of CANADA becomes ST. 'diamonds' looks like jewels to go with 'stone', but it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-type card game played over a series of deals, each a hand.

clue.text: Small body of troops elite, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals that the word for elite is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: picked troops are elite, hand-chosen ones

explanation.surface: A small crack unit is reputed to be the best.
explanation.walkthrough: This spelling of PICKET, a small detachment of soldiers, is said like 'picked'.
explanation.definitionFit: A picket, also spelt this way, is a small detachment of troops posted as a guard or outpost.

clue.text: Man sacred for Coleridge

parts.note: in Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan the sacred river is named: R for river
Alph is the sacred river of Kubla Khan, in the line 'Where Alph, the sacred river, ran'

explanation.surface: A man held holy by the Romantic poet Coleridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge's 'Alph, the sacred river' gives both pieces: R for river and ALPH, its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph is a common male first name, so it is an example of a man.

clue.text: One utters volumes in bar with misplaced relish

parts.note: a pub is a bar

indicators.note: misplaced says the letters of relish are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone talks loudly in a pub, putting relish in the wrong spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utters' here means issues or puts into circulation, not speaks; 'misplaced' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm that issues books puts out volumes, and to utter can mean to put into circulation.

clue.text: In book, discovers marks of approval for crisp snacks

parts.note: reads means finds out by reading, discovers
ticks are marks showing something is right

explanation.surface: Someone finds approving marks in a book about crunchy nibbles.
explanation.walkthrough: B + READS + TICKS; 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadsticks are thin, crunchy sticks of baked dough eaten as a snack.

clue.text: Daisy, perhaps, not quite monkshood

indicators.note: not quite says the final letter of the hood is dropped

parts.note: read as monk's hood, a cowl

explanation.surface: Daisy, perhaps not quite a monkshood (a poisonous flower).
explanation.walkthrough: Monkshood is a plant, which suits 'Daisy', but read it as monk's hood: COWL, less its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Daisy is a traditional name for a dairy animal, so a bovine is an example of a Daisy.

clue.text: Courts may decline following precedent

indicators.note: decline says the letters of courts may fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Law courts might refuse to follow earlier rulings.
explanation.walkthrough: COURTS MAY rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: What is customary follows established custom, so it follows precedent.

clue.text: Inane mistake, having sound truck, for girl not to go to Douglas

definitions.text: girl not to go to Douglas

indicators.note: mistake marks inane as letters to be rearranged
sound means the word for truck is taken as heard

parts.note: a lorry is the British word for a truck

explanation.surface: A silly error involving a loudspeaker van stops a girl visiting Douglas.
explanation.walkthrough: INANE rearranged gives ANNIE; 'sound' makes LORRY into LAURIE. In the Scottish song, Annie Laurie married another man rather than the poet William Douglas.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's heroine was courted by William Douglas but married someone else, so she never went to him.

clue.text: Prohibit man trailing round big star

indicators.note: trailing round says the man goes all round the word for prohibit

parts.note: Alan is a man's name
to debar is to prohibit or shut out

explanation.surface: Ban a man who follows a big celebrity around.
explanation.walkthrough: AL(DEBAR)AN. Aldebaran is the bright red giant in Taurus.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldebaran is a red giant, the brightest star in the constellation Taurus.

clue.text: Unable to sustain effort, was supported carrying another identical daughter

indicators.note: carrying says the word for was supported holds the other pieces

parts.note: shored means propped up, was supported
a twin is another, identical one

explanation.surface: Someone who tires easily, propped up while carrying a twin daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: SHOR(TWIN D)ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short of breath leaves one unable to keep up physical exertion for long.

clue.text: Withdraw in reverse order to remote area

indicators.note: in reverse order says the two words of the phrase meaning withdraw are swapped

parts.note: to back out is to withdraw: the second word
back, the first word of back out

explanation.surface: Retreat backwards to somewhere far away.
explanation.walkthrough: BACK OUT means withdraw; swap its words. The outback is the remote Australian interior.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian outback is the sparsely populated, remote interior of the country.

clue.text: Quaker Elizabeth's young children

definitions.meaning: Elizabeth ... was the Quaker prison reformer
small ... are young children, as ... are young fish

explanation.definitionFit: The reformer's surname, and a word for young fish used jokingly of little children.

clue.text: Father, spry but not robust

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
agile means spry, nimble

explanation.surface: A priest is lively but not strong.
explanation.walkthrough: FR + AGILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fragile is delicate and easily broken, the opposite of sturdy.

clue.text: Where orthodox Stalinist hurled anathemas without a break

definitions.meaning: playfully, a Stalinist condemned those on the Trotskyist side

explanation.walkthrough: Trot is short for Trotskyist, the faction Stalinists denounced.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means consecutively, one after another, with no pause between.

clue.text: What Orwell's animals were, just the same

definitions.meaning: in Animal Farm, all animals are this, though some are more so than others

explanation.definitionFit: The Animal Farm slogan declares all animals alike in status, and the word means identical in value.

clue.text: Iain's fine line in noisy quarrel

parts.note: braw is Scots for fine, and Iain is a Scottish name

explanation.surface: A Scot's good handwriting gets caught up in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAW is Scottish for fine or splendid; the Scottish name Iain marks it.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl is a rowdy fight or noisy quarrel.

clue.text: Gentle illumination.

definitions.meaning: brightness from the sun or a lamp

explanation.definitionFit: The word means mild or delicate, and also the brightness that makes things visible.

clue.text: Normally how one might take a calibrated rod

definitions.text: how one might take a calibrated rod
definitions.meaning: a graduated measuring rod is taken ...

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means usually or generally, and literally describes treating a marked rod as a ruler.

clue.text: Aim to get the last of the prawn salad

indicators.note: the last of says each of the following words gives its final letter

explanation.surface: Trying to grab the remaining bit of seafood salad.
explanation.walkthrough: Last letters of 'the prawn salad'.
explanation.definitionFit: An end is a goal or purpose, as in an end in itself.

clue.text: Doing the twist, being a sport

definitions.meaning: twisting into a coil or spiral
the winter game of sliding stones on ice

explanation.definitionFit: The word means twisting into coils, and is also a sport played with stones on ice.

clue.text: In meadow, turning fine for countryman

indicators.note: In says the word for fine goes inside the turned meadow
turning says the word for meadow is read backwards

parts.note: a ley (or lea) is a meadow
OK means fine

explanation.surface: Somewhere in a field, a rustic decides all is well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' gives YEL, and 'In' puts the word for fine inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A yokel is an unsophisticated rustic, a countryman in the disparaging sense.

clue.text: Remove money from nightclubs — time to admit error

indicators.note: to admit says the clubs and time take in the error

parts.note: dives are seedy nightclubs
a sin is a moral error

explanation.surface: Withdrawing funds from nightclubs, it is time to own up to a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: DI(SIN)VES + T.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinvest is to withdraw capital from an enterprise, removing one's money.
